### Applied Psychology

[appliedPsychology.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/appliedPsychology/appliedPsychology.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how psychological evidence informs education, workplaces, health and communities.

### Attention and Consciousness

Groups: 3 · Skills: 13

[attentionAndConsciousness.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/attentionAndConsciousness/attentionAndConsciousness.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Not all available information receives equal processing or enters reportable awareness. Focus, automaticity, waking states, and sleep have related but distinct psychological mechanisms.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how attention, awareness and sleep affect mental processing.

### Biological Foundations of Behavior

Groups: 4 · Skills: 17

[biologicalFoundationsOfBehavior.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/biologicalFoundationsOfBehavior/biologicalFoundationsOfBehavior.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Neural, endocrine, genetic, and evolved processes influence experience and action through interaction with environments. This field emphasizes explanatory mechanisms rather than rote anatomical detail or biological determinism.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how brains, hormones, inherited traits and environments influence behavior.

### Emotion and Psychological Regulation

Groups: 4 · Skills: 19

[emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation/emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how emotions arise, communicate information and can be managed.

#### Emotional Processes

Skills: 5

[emotionalProcesses.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation/emotionalProcesses/emotionalProcesses.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover the functions, bodily responses and interpretations involved in emotion.

##### Emotion Functions

[emotionFunctions.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation/emotionalProcesses/skills/emotionFunctions.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how emotions help signal needs, threats and opportunities.

##### Emotion Theories

[emotionTheories.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation/emotionalProcesses/skills/emotionTheories.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare theories describing how feelings and bodily responses relate.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how interpreting a situation influences emotional response.

[moodAndEmotion.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation/emotionalProcesses/skills/moodAndEmotion.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish a short emotional episode from a longer-lasting mood.

##### Physiology of Emotion

[physiologyOfEmotion.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation/emotionalProcesses/skills/physiologyOfEmotion.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize bodily changes that can accompany different emotional states.

#### Recognition and Expression

[recognitionAndExpression.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation/recognitionAndExpression/recognitionAndExpression.data.ts)

##### Cultural Variation in Expression

[culturalVariationInExpression.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation/recognitionAndExpression/skills/culturalVariationInExpression.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how social and cultural rules affect emotional expression.

[emotionVocabulary.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation/recognitionAndExpression/skills/emotionVocabulary.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Differentiate related affective states to communicate distinctions in intensity, quality, or cause.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use words that describe emotional experiences precisely.

##### Emotional Self-Awareness

[emotionalSelfAwareness.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/emotionAndPsychologicalRegulation/recognitionAndExpression/skills/emotionalSelfAwareness.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify feelings, accompanying sensations, and possible triggers without assuming a single interpretation is certain.

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how a person's interpretation of demands and resources shapes experienced strain.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how interpreting demands influences stress responses.

### Learning and Behavior Change

Groups: 4 · Skills: 19

[learningAndBehaviorChange.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/learningAndBehaviorChange.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Past experience modifies responding through predictive cues, consequences, and social observation. This domain explains mechanisms of behavioral acquisition and flexibility rather than memory storage or a teaching sequence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how experience, consequences and observation change behavior over time.

#### Operant Learning

Skills: 6

[operantLearning.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/operantLearning/operantLearning.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how rewards and consequences influence behavior.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when removing something desirable discourages a behavior.

[negativeReinforcement.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/operantLearning/skills/negativeReinforcement.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify a consequence removed after a behavior that increases future responding, without confusing removal with punishment.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how removing an unpleasant condition can strengthen behavior.

##### Operant Conditioning

[operantConditioning.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/operantLearning/skills/operantConditioning.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how actions change according to their consequences.

##### Positive Punishment

[positivePunishment.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/operantLearning/skills/positivePunishment.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when adding a consequence reduces the chance of an action.

##### Positive Reinforcement

[positiveReinforcement.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/operantLearning/skills/positiveReinforcement.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify a consequence added after a behavior that increases its future occurrence under the relevant conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when adding a desirable consequence makes behavior more likely.

##### Reinforcement Schedules

[reinforcementSchedules.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/operantLearning/skills/reinforcementSchedules.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how a conditioned response develops through repeated pairings.

[stimulusDiscrimination.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/respondentConditioning/skills/stimulusDiscrimination.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how people distinguish a learned signal from other stimuli.

[stimulusGeneralization.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/respondentConditioning/skills/stimulusGeneralization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why a response acquired for one cue may also occur with similar but untrained cues.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why similar signals can trigger a learned response.

Skills: 3

[socialLearning.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/socialLearning/socialLearning.data.ts)

[observationalLearning.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/socialLearning/skills/observationalLearning.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how people can learn behavior by watching others.

[vicariousReinforcement.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/socialLearning/skills/vicariousReinforcement.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize why seeing someone else rewarded can influence behavior.

[transferAndBehavioralFlexibility.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/transferAndBehavioralFlexibility/transferAndBehavioralFlexibility.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Acquired responses must generalize appropriately across contexts while remaining sensitive to meaningful differences.

##### Context-Dependent Learning

[contextDependentLearning.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/transferAndBehavioralFlexibility/skills/contextDependentLearning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why a response learned in one setting may not transfer unchanged to another.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when learning depends strongly on the setting where it occurred.

##### Feedback and Skill Acquisition

[feedbackAndSkillAcquisition.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/transferAndBehavioralFlexibility/skills/feedbackAndSkillAcquisition.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how informative outcome feedback changes later performance differently from simple repetition.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how informative feedback helps people improve a skill.

##### Learned Helplessness

[learnedHelplessness.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/transferAndBehavioralFlexibility/skills/learnedHelplessness.data.ts)

[transferOfLearning.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/learningAndBehaviorChange/transferAndBehavioralFlexibility/skills/transferOfLearning.data.ts)

### Mental Health and Clinical Science

Groups: 4 · Skills: 17

[mentalHealthAndClinicalScience.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/mentalHealthAndClinicalScience/mentalHealthAndClinicalScience.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Clinical psychology investigates distress, impaired functioning, and evidence-based assessment and intervention. Learning these concepts does not authorize students to diagnose themselves or others, deliver therapy, or replace qualified professional care.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore psychological wellbeing, mental-health difficulties and professional care through evidence.

#### Assessment and Professional Support

[assessmentAndProfessionalSupport.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/mentalHealthAndClinicalScience/assessmentAndProfessionalSupport/assessmentAndProfessionalSupport.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Clinical decisions use trained judgment, validated measures, and context; ethical education focuses on how professional care works rather than practicing diagnosis.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how trained professionals assess difficulties and provide support.

[clinicalFormulation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/mentalHealthAndClinicalScience/assessmentAndProfessionalSupport/skills/clinicalFormulation.data.ts)

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how clinicians combine evidence to develop a provisional explanation.

##### Clinical Interview Purpose

[clinicalInterviewPurpose.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/mentalHealthAndClinicalScience/assessmentAndProfessionalSupport/skills/clinicalInterviewPurpose.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain what a structured history can contribute to understanding a person's reported difficulties and context.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore what a clinical interview can reveal about a person's experiences and context.

[professionalRolesAndReferral.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/mentalHealthAndClinicalScience/assessmentAndProfessionalSupport/skills/professionalRolesAndReferral.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish roles of psychological practitioners and medical professionals and identify why appropriate referral may be needed.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when different kinds of qualified professionals or referrals are needed.

[psychologicalScreeningVersusDiagnosis.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/mentalHealthAndClinicalScience/assessmentAndProfessionalSupport/skills/psychologicalScreeningVersusDiagnosis.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish preliminary indicators from comprehensive professional assessment.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish an initial screening result from a professional diagnosis.

#### Intervention Evidence and Ethics

Skills: 4

[interventionEvidenceAndEthics.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/mentalHealthAndClinicalScience/interventionEvidenceAndEthics/interventionEvidenceAndEthics.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Treatment approaches propose different mechanisms and require evaluation for effectiveness, suitability, potential harm, and professional standards.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why treatment claims require evidence, safeguards and professional ethics.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn why supported exposure approaches require suitable professional oversight.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand the principles behind cognitive and behavioral treatment approaches.

[evaluatingTreatmentClaims.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/mentalHealthAndClinicalScience/interventionEvidenceAndEthics/skills/evaluatingTreatmentClaims.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess evidence from controlled studies, meaningful outcomes, adverse effects, and follow-up rather than testimonials or guaranteed-cure marketing.

**User-friendly description (en):** Evaluate treatment claims using studies and outcomes rather than testimonials.

[therapeuticAlliance.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/mentalHealthAndClinicalScience/interventionEvidenceAndEthics/skills/therapeuticAlliance.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why collaboration, trust, and agreement on goals matter for outcomes across psychological therapies.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how trust and cooperation contribute to therapeutic care.

Distinguish clinical evaluation from ordinary developmental variation without diagnosing people from isolated traits.

### Motivation, Goals, and Habits

Groups: 3 · Skills: 16

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why people act, pursue goals and develop automatic routines.

Skills: 7

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish a person's general self-evaluation from specific abilities.

##### Self-Serving Attributions

[selfServingAttributions.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/personalityAndIndividualVariation/selfConceptAndIdentity/skills/selfServingAttributions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how explanations of successes and failures may protect a favorable self-image.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when people take credit for success but blame circumstances for failure.

#### Traits and Personality Models

Skills: 5

[traitsAndPersonalityModels.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/personalityAndIndividualVariation/traitsAndPersonalityModels/traitsAndPersonalityModels.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Trait models summarize recurring behavioral tendencies while leaving room for situational variation and change.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how personality traits are described and assessed.

##### Big Five Trait Model

[bigFiveTraitModel.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/personalityAndIndividualVariation/traitsAndPersonalityModels/skills/bigFiveTraitModel.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the five broad personality dimensions as descriptive continua rather than categorical diagnoses.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand the five broad dimensions used in a common personality model.

##### Personality Assessment

[personalityAssessment.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/personalityAndIndividualVariation/traitsAndPersonalityModels/skills/personalityAssessment.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate self-report and informant measures for reliability, validity, and response distortion.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore what personality tests can and cannot measure reliably.

##### Personality Stability and Change

[personalityStabilityAndChange.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/personalityAndIndividualVariation/traitsAndPersonalityModels/skills/personalityStabilityAndChange.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain both rank-order consistency and mean-level changes across the lifespan.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why some personality tendencies persist while others change.

##### Trait–Situation Interaction

[traitSituationInteraction.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/personalityAndIndividualVariation/traitsAndPersonalityModels/skills/traitSituationInteraction.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analyze why the same person may behave differently under different incentives or social demands.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how personality and situation jointly affect behavior.

##### Trait versus State

[traitVersusState.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/personalityAndIndividualVariation/traitsAndPersonalityModels/skills/traitVersusState.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish relatively stable tendencies from temporary conditions affecting behavior.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish a lasting personality tendency from a temporary state.

### Psychological Science and Inquiry

Groups: 5 · Skills: 31

[psychologicalScienceAndInquiry.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Psychology explains behavior and mental processes through empirical evidence, multiple levels of analysis, and ethical inquiry. Its explanations are provisional and require stronger support than anecdote or authority.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how psychologists investigate behavior and mental processes through careful research.

#### Evidence and Interpretation

Skills: 6

[evidenceAndInterpretation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/evidenceAndInterpretation/evidenceAndInterpretation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Quantitative summaries and research transparency help discriminate robust patterns from noise and misleading causal stories.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how evidence and transparent analysis support research conclusions.

##### Analytical Reproducibility

[analyticalReproducibility.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/evidenceAndInterpretation/skills/analyticalReproducibility.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why access to reported methods, data, and analytic decisions allows independent verification of a result.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize why clear methods and analysis choices allow independent checking.

##### Confounding Variables

[confoundingVariables.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/evidenceAndInterpretation/skills/confoundingVariables.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify background factors that move with a proposed cause and could produce an observed group difference.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify other factors that might explain a difference between groups.

##### Correlation and Causation

[correlationAndCausation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/evidenceAndInterpretation/skills/correlationAndCausation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Consider reversed direction and third-variable explanations when two psychological measures vary together.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish association from evidence that one psychological factor causes another.

##### Descriptive Statistics in Research

[descriptiveStatisticsInResearch.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/evidenceAndInterpretation/skills/descriptiveStatisticsInResearch.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret distributions, typical values, and variability without treating a group average as every participant's experience.

**User-friendly description (en):** Read typical values and variation without assuming everyone matches the average.

##### Evidence Quality

[evidenceQuality.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/evidenceAndInterpretation/skills/evidenceQuality.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Weigh converging studies, effect magnitude, uncertainty, and publication bias instead of relying on one striking result.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare research findings by their strength, uncertainty and possible biases.

##### Study Replication

[studyReplication.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/evidenceAndInterpretation/skills/studyReplication.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why repeating a psychological investigation with new observations helps assess the robustness and generality of a result.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why repeating a study helps test whether a finding is robust.

#### Foundations and Perspectives

Skills: 4

[foundationsAndPerspectives.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/foundationsAndPerspectives/foundationsAndPerspectives.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Scientific accounts distinguish description, prediction, and causal explanation while combining cognitive, biological, behavioral, and sociocultural perspectives.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover different perspectives and scientific goals in psychology.

##### Explanation and Prediction

[explanationAndPrediction.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/foundationsAndPerspectives/skills/explanationAndPrediction.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Separate a description of observed behavior, a forecast about future behavior, and a proposed mechanism responsible for it.

**User-friendly description (en):** Separate describing behavior from predicting or explaining its causes.

##### Historical Psychological Approaches

[historicalPsychologicalApproaches.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/foundationsAndPerspectives/skills/historicalPsychologicalApproaches.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate foundational schools of thought in their historical context and assess why some claims have been revised by later evidence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how early psychological theories evolved as evidence improved.

##### Psychological Perspectives

[psychologicalPerspectives.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/foundationsAndPerspectives/skills/psychologicalPerspectives.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare how behavioral, cognitive, biological, developmental, and sociocultural models explain different aspects of the same phenomenon.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare how different psychological approaches explain the same behavior.

##### Scope of Psychological Science

[scopeOfPsychologicalScience.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/foundationsAndPerspectives/skills/scopeOfPsychologicalScience.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish the empirical study of behavior and experience from philosophical evaluation of arguments and from medical diagnosis or treatment.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish psychological research from philosophy and clinical treatment.

#### Measurement and Sampling

Skills: 5

[measurementAndSampling.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/measurementAndSampling/measurementAndSampling.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Operational measures offer imperfect indicators of psychological constructs, and recruitment choices limit generalization.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how psychologists measure constructs and choose research participants.

##### Construct Validity

[constructValidity.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/measurementAndSampling/skills/constructValidity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess whether a test actually captures the intended psychological attribute rather than a convenient proxy.

**User-friendly description (en):** Evaluate whether a test captures the concept it claims to measure.

##### Measurement Bias

[measurementBias.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/measurementAndSampling/skills/measurementBias.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify systematic distortions from test wording, cultural assumptions, inaccessible formats, or observer expectations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Find ways a measurement could systematically disadvantage or misrepresent people.

##### Operational Definitions

[operationalDefinitions.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/measurementAndSampling/skills/operationalDefinitions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Translate an abstract concept such as stress or attention into an observable indicator and identify what it leaves out.

**User-friendly description (en):** Translate an abstract psychological idea into observable measurements.

##### Reliability of Measures

[reliabilityOfMeasures.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/measurementAndSampling/skills/reliabilityOfMeasures.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate whether repeated or equivalent measurements are consistent enough for their intended interpretation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Check whether a psychological measure gives consistent results.

##### Representative Sampling

[representativeSampling.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/measurementAndSampling/skills/representativeSampling.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how sampling, recruitment, and nonresponse affect the generalizability of findings.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how recruiting a sample limits conclusions about a population.

#### Research Ethics

Skills: 7

[researchEthics.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/researchEthics/researchEthics.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Studies involving people must respect autonomy, dignity, safety, and confidentiality, including additional safeguards for vulnerable participants.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how research can respect people's autonomy, dignity and safety.

##### Deception in Research

[deceptionInResearch.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/researchEthics/skills/deceptionInResearch.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Evaluate the rare conditions under which incomplete disclosure might be ethically defensible given oversight, scientific necessity, and risks.

**User-friendly description (en):** Consider when withholding information in research might be ethically defensible.

##### Informed Consent

[informedConsent.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/researchEthics/skills/informedConsent.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify the information required for a voluntary decision to participate, including procedures, foreseeable risks, and withdrawal.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize what participants should know before agreeing to join a study.

##### Research Anonymity

[researchAnonymity.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/researchEthics/skills/researchAnonymity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain when collected data cannot be linked to a participant and why this differs from merely promising confidentiality.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish anonymous research data from information kept confidential.

##### Research Confidentiality

[researchConfidentiality.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/researchEthics/skills/researchConfidentiality.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how identifiable participant information may be protected through access restrictions and careful reporting.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how researchers protect identifiable participant data.

##### Research Debriefing

[researchDebriefing.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/researchEthics/skills/researchDebriefing.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the purpose of a meaningful post-participation explanation and support when a study withheld important information.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why researchers sometimes need to debrief people after a study.

##### Research with Vulnerable Participants

[researchWithVulnerableParticipants.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/researchEthics/skills/researchWithVulnerableParticipants.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain additional assent, consent, power-balance, and accessibility considerations involving children or dependent groups.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize additional protections needed for children and vulnerable participants.

##### Risk–Benefit Assessment

[riskBenefitAssessment.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/researchEthics/skills/riskBenefitAssessment.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify possible distress, coercion, stigma, and privacy harms and consider less intrusive alternatives.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare potential research benefits with risks of distress, harm or coercion.

#### Study Designs

Skills: 9

[studyDesigns.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/studyDesigns/studyDesigns.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Different ways of collecting evidence answer different questions and support different levels of causal inference.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn why different research designs support different conclusions.

##### Blinding in Research

[blindingInResearch.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/studyDesigns/skills/blindingInResearch.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how keeping condition assignments unknown to participants or evaluators can reduce some sources of bias, and why blinding is not universally possible.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how blinding participants or evaluators can reduce certain biases.

##### Controlled Experiments

[controlledExperiments.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/studyDesigns/skills/controlledExperiments.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify manipulated variables, outcome measures, comparison conditions, and the logic of an experimental contrast.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify manipulated factors, measured outcomes and controls in an experiment.

##### Correlational Studies

[correlationalStudies.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/studyDesigns/skills/correlationalStudies.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Determine what an association between measured variables reveals without treating co-occurrence as proof of cause.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize what correlations show and what they cannot prove.

##### Expectation Effects

[expectationEffects.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/studyDesigns/skills/expectationEffects.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how beliefs about an intervention or condition can change reported experience or behavior independently of its specific mechanism.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how expectations can influence behavior or reported experience.

##### Questionnaire Research

[questionnaireResearch.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/studyDesigns/skills/questionnaireResearch.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret structured self-reports while considering item wording, response scales, and socially desirable answers.

**User-friendly description (en):** Interpret questionnaires while accounting for wording and response bias.

##### Random Assignment

[randomAssignment.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/studyDesigns/skills/randomAssignment.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how chance allocation to conditions reduces systematic differences without confusing it with population sampling.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how random assignment can make study groups more comparable.

##### Research Interviews

[researchInterviews.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/studyDesigns/skills/researchInterviews.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret conversational accounts of experience while considering interviewer influence, recall limits, and unequal disclosure pressures.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore what interviews can reveal and how questions influence responses.

##### Researchable Hypotheses

[researchableHypotheses.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/studyDesigns/skills/researchableHypotheses.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Transform a broad statement about human behavior into a claim with observable variables and possible disconfirming evidence.

**User-friendly description (en):** Turn an everyday claim about behavior into a researchable hypothesis.

##### Systematic Observation

[systematicObservation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/psychologicalScienceAndInquiry/studyDesigns/skills/systematicObservation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Use predefined behavioral categories to distinguish structured observations from informal personal impressions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Record behavior using consistent observation rules rather than impressions.

### Sensation and Perception

Groups: 5 · Skills: 23

[sensationAndPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/sensationAndPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Sensory information is detected, selected, organized, and interpreted into an experienced world. Psychological perception differs from simple measurement of physical stimuli or anatomy of sense organs.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how sensory signals become experiences of the world around us.

#### Body and Chemical Senses

Skills: 6

[bodyAndChemicalSenses.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/bodyAndChemicalSenses/bodyAndChemicalSenses.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Touch, pain, balance, body position, smell, and taste rely on partly distinct receptor and processing pathways. Their psychological importance lies in how signals become conscious experiences and guide action, not in cataloguing anatomy alone.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how touch, pain, smell, taste and body senses guide experience.

##### Pain Perception

[painPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/bodyAndChemicalSenses/skills/painPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how nociceptive input, context, attention, and expectations interact in the experience of pain, without equating its intensity with a single tissue measurement.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why pain experience depends on more than one tissue signal.

##### Proprioception

[proprioception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/bodyAndChemicalSenses/skills/proprioception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how information about muscle and joint state supports awareness of limb position and movement even without vision.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how your body senses limb position without looking.

##### Smell Perception

[smellPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/bodyAndChemicalSenses/skills/smellPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Describe how patterns of odorant stimulation contribute to identifying smells and why learning, adaptation, and context can alter odor judgments.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how prior experience and context affect identifying smells.

##### Taste Perception

[tastePerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/bodyAndChemicalSenses/skills/tastePerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how gustatory information supports basic taste qualities and interacts with smell and other sensory cues in experienced flavor.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how taste and smell combine to create flavor.

##### Touch Perception

[touchPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/bodyAndChemicalSenses/skills/touchPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how contact, pressure, vibration, and texture are discriminated through somatosensory processing, and why perceived touch depends on stimulus location and context.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how pressure and vibration become the experience of touch.

##### Vestibular Perception

[vestibularPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/bodyAndChemicalSenses/skills/vestibularPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how sensed head motion and orientation contribute to balance and spatial perception, including interactions with vision and proprioception.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how head movement and orientation help maintain balance.

#### Illusions and Multisensory Perception

Skills: 4

[illusionsAndMultisensoryPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/illusionsAndMultisensoryPerception/illusionsAndMultisensoryPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Systematic distortions and interactions across senses reveal how perception infers likely causes of stimulation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover what sensory illusions reveal about how perception works.

##### Cross-Modal Integration

[crossModalIntegration.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/illusionsAndMultisensoryPerception/skills/crossModalIntegration.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how combined sensory cues can modify a percept compared with cues considered separately.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how cues from different senses change the same experience.

##### Eyewitness Perception

[eyewitnessPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/illusionsAndMultisensoryPerception/skills/eyewitnessPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess the effects of attention, conditions, and later interpretation on the reliability of witnessed events.

**User-friendly description (en):** Consider the limits of eyewitness observations under distracting conditions.

##### Perceptual Expectations

[perceptualExpectations.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/illusionsAndMultisensoryPerception/skills/perceptualExpectations.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analyze the influence of prior knowledge or priming while distinguishing interpretation from the actual stimulus.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when prior knowledge changes interpretation of an unchanged stimulus.

##### Visual Illusions

[visualIllusions.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/illusionsAndMultisensoryPerception/skills/visualIllusions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how contextual cues create reliable differences between an object's measured property and its appearance.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why a visual illusion can differ from a measured physical feature.

#### Perceptual Organization

Skills: 4

[perceptualOrganization.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/perceptualOrganization/perceptualOrganization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** The mind uses grouping cues and expectations to construct coherent objects from ambiguous sensory input.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn how the mind groups sensory information into recognizable objects.

##### Bottom-Up and Top-Down Processing

[bottomUpAndTopDownProcessing.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/perceptualOrganization/skills/bottomUpAndTopDownProcessing.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish stimulus-driven evidence from prior expectations and explain their interaction in perception.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how expectations and incoming sensations jointly shape perception.

##### Figure–Ground Organization

[figureGroundOrganization.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/perceptualOrganization/skills/figureGroundOrganization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify how context changes which part of a scene is experienced as a foreground object.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize which parts of a scene appear as foreground or background.

##### Gestalt Grouping

[gestaltGrouping.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/perceptualOrganization/skills/gestaltGrouping.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Apply similarity, proximity, closure, and continuity to explain grouping of visible elements.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use proximity, similarity and continuity to explain visual grouping.

##### Perceptual Constancy

[perceptualConstancy.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/perceptualOrganization/skills/perceptualConstancy.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain relatively stable perceived size, shape, or color across changing sensory conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why size, shape or color can seem stable under changing conditions.

#### Sensory Detection

Skills: 5

[sensoryDetection.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/sensoryDetection/sensoryDetection.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Sensitivity depends on stimulus intensity, adaptation, and detection conditions rather than a perfectly fixed threshold.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how the strength and conditions of stimulation affect detection.

##### Detection Thresholds

[detectionThresholds.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/sensoryDetection/skills/detectionThresholds.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how signal strength and competing noise affect the likelihood of noticing a stimulus.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why stronger signals may be easier to notice amid noise.

##### Difference Thresholds

[differenceThresholds.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/sensoryDetection/skills/differenceThresholds.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate the detectable difference between stimuli to their starting intensity and context.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when a difference between two stimuli becomes noticeable.

##### Sensation versus Perception

[sensationVersusPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/sensoryDetection/skills/sensationVersusPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish sensory encoding of stimulation from the interpretation of what that stimulation represents.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish detecting a stimulus from interpreting what it means.

##### Sensory Adaptation

[sensoryAdaptation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/sensoryDetection/skills/sensoryAdaptation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Describe changed sensitivity after sustained stimulation without mistaking it for change in the source.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how sensitivity can change after exposure to a constant stimulus.

##### Sensory Transduction

[sensoryTransduction.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/sensoryDetection/skills/sensoryTransduction.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how sensory receptors transform light, mechanical stimulation, or chemical signals into neural activity, distinguishing this initial encoding from later perception.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how sensory receptors convert stimulation into neural signals.

#### Visual and Auditory Experience

Skills: 4

[visualAndAuditoryExperience.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/visualAndAuditoryExperience/visualAndAuditoryExperience.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Spatial, chromatic, and speech experiences emerge from interpreting patterns of visual or acoustic information.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how we interpret visual and auditory patterns.

##### Color Perception

[colorPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/visualAndAuditoryExperience/skills/colorPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate wavelengths, relative context, and neural processing to perceived colors without equating color with one wavelength.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why perceived color depends on context and neural processing.

##### Depth Perception

[depthPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/visualAndAuditoryExperience/skills/depthPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain the contributions of binocular and monocular cues to estimating distance.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify visual cues that help us judge how far away something is.

##### Sound Localization

[soundLocalization.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/visualAndAuditoryExperience/skills/soundLocalization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how timing and level differences between ears contribute to perceived sound direction.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how differences between ears help locate a sound.

##### Speech Perception

[speechPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/sensationAndPerception/visualAndAuditoryExperience/skills/speechPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analyze how acoustic cues, noise, and language expectations shape understanding of spoken messages.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how sound and language expectations affect speech understanding.

### Social Psychology

Groups: 4 · Skills: 24

[socialPsychology.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/socialPsychology.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Thought and behavior change in the actual or imagined presence of others. Social processes involve interpretation, group membership, influence, and relationships without assuming all people respond alike.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how other people influence our beliefs, actions and relationships.

#### Group Dynamics

Skills: 5

[groupDynamics.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/groupDynamics/groupDynamics.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Belonging and coordination can alter performance, responsibility, intergroup attitudes, and collective decisions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how group identities and discussions shape behavior.

##### Bystander Effect

[bystanderEffect.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/groupDynamics/skills/bystanderEffect.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how others' presence can change perceived responsibility or interpretations of a situation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why people may hesitate to help when many others are present.

##### Group Polarization

[groupPolarization.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/groupDynamics/skills/groupPolarization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Describe how discussion among similarly inclined people can shift collective judgments toward more extreme positions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why group discussion can make shared positions more extreme.

##### Groupthink

[groupthink.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/groupDynamics/skills/groupthink.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify pressures toward unanimity that discourage dissent and reduce the scrutiny of alternatives.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when pressure for agreement prevents critical evaluation in a group.

##### In-Group and Out-Group Bias

[inGroupAndOutGroupBias.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/groupDynamics/skills/inGroupAndOutGroupBias.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analyze unequal evaluation of people based on group membership even without direct personal experience.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize unjustified favoritism toward one's own group.

##### Social Identity

[socialIdentity.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/groupDynamics/skills/socialIdentity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how membership in meaningful groups contributes to self-description and intergroup interpretation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how belonging to a group influences social identity.

#### Influence and Persuasion

Skills: 6

[influenceAndPersuasion.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/influenceAndPersuasion/influenceAndPersuasion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Other people's behavior, claims, and group norms can shift beliefs or actions through identifiable social mechanisms.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how groups, authority and messages influence choices.

##### Conformity

[conformity.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/influenceAndPersuasion/skills/conformity.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain changes in expressed judgments or behavior under perceived group pressure.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize changes in behavior made to match a group's expectations.

##### Informational Social Influence

[informationalSocialInfluence.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/influenceAndPersuasion/skills/informationalSocialInfluence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain adopting others' judgments when they appear to provide useful evidence about uncertainty.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand when others provide information we use to guide decisions.

##### Normative Social Influence

[normativeSocialInfluence.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/influenceAndPersuasion/skills/normativeSocialInfluence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain compliance motivated by social approval or avoidance of rejection.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when the desire to fit in changes a person's behavior.

##### Obedience to Authority

[obedienceToAuthority.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/influenceAndPersuasion/skills/obedienceToAuthority.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analyze how authority cues and situational pressures influence compliance, including ethical limits of classic research.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why authority can influence decisions without guaranteeing correctness.

##### Persuasion Routes

[persuasionRoutes.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/influenceAndPersuasion/skills/persuasionRoutes.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare careful evaluation of arguments with reliance on source or presentation cues.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare different routes through which persuasive messages influence attitudes.

##### Recognizing Psychological Manipulation

[recognizingPsychologicalManipulation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/influenceAndPersuasion/skills/recognizingPsychologicalManipulation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify exploitative uses of urgency, isolation, guilt, or unequal power without teaching techniques to manipulate others.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify pressure tactics that exploit fear, guilt or social expectations.

#### Relationships and Communication

Skills: 7

[relationshipsAndCommunication.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/relationshipsAndCommunication/relationshipsAndCommunication.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relationships develop through mutual interpretation, reciprocal actions, boundaries, and social context rather than perfect reading of another's intentions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Learn to recognize healthy communication, boundaries and relational challenges.

##### Active Listening

[activeListening.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/relationshipsAndCommunication/skills/activeListening.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish checking understanding and attending to another person's meaning from merely waiting to reply.

**User-friendly description (en):** Practice attending to and clarifying what someone is communicating.

##### Attachment in Relationships

[attachmentInRelationships.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/relationshipsAndCommunication/skills/attachmentInRelationships.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how expectations about availability and support can influence close relationships while avoiding rigid labeling of individuals.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how attachment patterns can influence relationships over time.

##### Interpersonal Conflict

[interpersonalConflict.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/relationshipsAndCommunication/skills/interpersonalConflict.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analyze how unmet expectations, differing interpretations, communication patterns, and situational pressures contribute to the emergence or escalation of disagreements between people.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how disagreements escalate or can be resolved constructively.

##### Nonverbal Communication

[nonverbalCommunication.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/relationshipsAndCommunication/skills/nonverbalCommunication.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Interpret gesture, tone, and interpersonal distance in cultural and situational context rather than through universal decoding rules.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how facial expression, gesture and tone convey information.

##### Personal Boundaries

[personalBoundaries.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/relationshipsAndCommunication/skills/personalBoundaries.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how individuals express limits about interactions, information, and bodily or emotional space, and how those limits merit respect.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify the limits a person sets around their body, time and information.

##### Relationship Repair

[relationshipRepair.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/relationshipsAndCommunication/skills/relationshipRepair.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how acknowledgment, apology, changed behavior, and negotiated expectations can help restore trust after interpersonal harm without assuming reconciliation is always safe or obligatory.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand what helps restore trust after a disagreement.

##### Voluntary Consent

[voluntaryConsent.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/relationshipsAndCommunication/skills/voluntaryConsent.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish an informed, freely given and revocable agreement from silence, coercion, or assumed permission.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand that consent must be voluntary and can be withdrawn.

#### Social Perception

Skills: 6

[socialPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/socialPerception/socialPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Judgments about other people are inferred from limited evidence and shaped by expectations, roles, and context.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how we interpret people's actions, intentions and feelings.

##### Compassion

[compassion.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/socialPerception/skills/compassion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain concern for another person's suffering accompanied by motivation to offer appropriate help, distinct from understanding alone.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish compassionate concern from simply understanding another's feelings.

##### Empathy

[empathy.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/socialPerception/skills/empathy.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain understanding or affectively responding to another person's possible experience while recognizing that one cannot know it with certainty.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand empathy as recognizing and sharing aspects of another's experience.

##### First Impressions

[firstImpressions.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/socialPerception/skills/firstImpressions.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how early information can disproportionately influence expectations about a person.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how first impressions form and why they can mislead.

##### Perspective Taking

[perspectiveTaking.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/socialPerception/skills/perspectiveTaking.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain inferring another person's possible viewpoint while recognizing that their actual experience remains uncertain.

**User-friendly description (en):** Practice considering a situation from someone else's perspective.

##### Social Attribution

[socialAttribution.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/socialPerception/skills/socialAttribution.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish explanations invoking a person's dispositions from those emphasizing circumstances and available choices.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how people infer causes of others' behavior.

##### Stereotype Activation

[stereotypeActivation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/socialPsychology/socialPerception/skills/stereotypeActivation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analyze how culturally available categories affect social perception without treating stereotypes as reliable descriptions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how stereotypes can influence judgments before conscious reflection.

### Thinking and Decision-Making

Groups: 5 · Skills: 27

[thinkingAndDecisionMaking.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/thinkingAndDecisionMaking.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Cognitive processes create concepts, guide inferences, solve problems, and select actions under limited information. The focus is what people actually do, not whether their reasoning satisfies a formal philosophical standard.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how people form concepts, solve problems and make imperfect decisions.

#### Choices Under Uncertainty

Skills: 5

[choicesUnderUncertainty.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/choicesUnderUncertainty/choicesUnderUncertainty.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Decisions depend on reference points, delayed consequences, uncertainty, and how alternatives are presented.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how uncertainty, probability and presentation influence choices.

##### Base-Rate Neglect

[baseRateNeglect.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/choicesUnderUncertainty/skills/baseRateNeglect.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain failures to incorporate prior frequencies when a compelling individual example is present.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when people overlook background frequencies in their judgments.

##### Choice Architecture

[choiceArchitecture.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/choicesUnderUncertainty/skills/choiceArchitecture.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify how defaults, option ordering, and information load shift behavior without assuming every nudge is harmless.

**User-friendly description (en):** See how defaults and arrangement of options can influence decisions.

##### Delay Discounting

[delayDiscounting.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/choicesUnderUncertainty/skills/delayDiscounting.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain changing subjective value of an outcome as its delivery becomes more distant.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why distant rewards can be valued less than immediate ones.

##### Loss Aversion

[lossAversion.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/choicesUnderUncertainty/skills/lossAversion.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why a loss relative to a reference point may carry greater subjective weight than an equivalent gain.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand why losses can feel more significant than equivalent gains.

##### Risk Perception

[riskPerception.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/choicesUnderUncertainty/skills/riskPerception.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analyze why vividness, familiarity, controllability, and dread affect judgments of risk.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize that perceived danger depends on more than statistical odds.

#### Heuristics and Biases

Skills: 7

[heuristicsAndBiases.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/heuristicsAndBiases/heuristicsAndBiases.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Fast judgments exploit convenient cues but may be systematically distorted by memory, presentation, or expectations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover shortcuts and biases that influence judgments.

##### Anchoring Bias

[anchoringBias.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/heuristicsAndBiases/skills/anchoringBias.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Describe how an initial number or reference shifts later quantitative estimates.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how an initial number can bias later judgments.

##### Availability Heuristic

[availabilityHeuristic.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/heuristicsAndBiases/skills/availabilityHeuristic.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain using the ease of recalling examples as a substitute for estimating real frequency.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain why easily recalled examples may seem more common.

##### Confirmation Bias

[confirmationBias.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/heuristicsAndBiases/skills/confirmationBias.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analyze selective search or interpretation of evidence that favors an existing belief.

**User-friendly description (en):** Identify the tendency to favor evidence supporting an existing belief.

##### Framing Effects

[framingEffects.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/heuristicsAndBiases/skills/framingEffects.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Assess how equivalent choices described differently can produce different judgments.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why describing equivalent choices differently can change decisions.

##### Fundamental Attribution Error

[fundamentalAttributionError.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/heuristicsAndBiases/skills/fundamentalAttributionError.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Describe overemphasizing dispositions and neglecting situational constraints when explaining another person's behavior.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when others' behavior is explained too strongly by their personality.

##### Hindsight Bias

[hindsightBias.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/heuristicsAndBiases/skills/hindsightBias.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain why knowing an outcome retrospectively makes it seem more predictable.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize why past outcomes can seem more predictable after they happen.

##### Representativeness Heuristic

[representativenessHeuristic.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/heuristicsAndBiases/skills/representativenessHeuristic.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain judging likelihood by resemblance to a familiar category while neglecting relevant background information.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when similarity to a stereotype replaces relevant probability.

[languageAndCognitiveAbilities.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/languageAndCognitiveAbilities/languageAndCognitiveAbilities.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Psychological research investigates language processing and performance differences rather than literary quality or innate worth.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how people process language and how cognitive abilities are measured.

**Methodological description (English):** Distinguish a measured score from a complete account of intellectual capacity, considering error and conditions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize what a cognitive test can and cannot tell us about someone.

##### Language Comprehension

[languageComprehension.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/languageAndCognitiveAbilities/skills/languageComprehension.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Relate context and prior knowledge to the interpretation of ambiguous expressions.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how listeners and readers build meaning from language.

##### Language Production

[languageProduction.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/languageAndCognitiveAbilities/skills/languageProduction.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain planning and word selection in speaking, including what errors reveal about processing.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how people plan and produce spoken or written language.

##### Theories of Intelligence

[theoriesOfIntelligence.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/languageAndCognitiveAbilities/skills/theoriesOfIntelligence.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Compare broad and domain-specific models and evaluate how well measures predict relevant outcomes.

**User-friendly description (en):** Compare different scientific theories about intelligence and abilities.

#### Mental Representation

Skills: 5

[mentalRepresentation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/mentalRepresentation/mentalRepresentation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Categories, schemas, and internal models compress information, enabling predictions while sometimes concealing important differences.

**User-friendly description (en):** Discover how mental concepts and representations organize information.

##### Cognitive Schemas

[cognitiveSchemas.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/mentalRepresentation/skills/cognitiveSchemas.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how organized expectations influence the interpretation of familiar situations.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how familiar mental structures affect expectations and interpretation.

##### Concept Formation

[conceptFormation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/mentalRepresentation/skills/conceptFormation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how shared features and distinguishing properties support useful mental categories.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explain how people learn which examples belong to a concept.

##### Exemplar-Based Categorization

[exemplarBasedCategorization.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/mentalRepresentation/skills/exemplarBasedCategorization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how classification can rely on comparisons with specific remembered category instances.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore how remembered individual examples shape classification.

##### Mental Models

[mentalModels.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/mentalRepresentation/skills/mentalModels.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Analyze how simplified internal representations predict outcomes and where neglected details cause errors.

**User-friendly description (en):** Use a mental model to reason about how a situation might work.

##### Prototype-Based Categorization

[prototypeBasedCategorization.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/mentalRepresentation/skills/prototypeBasedCategorization.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how classification can rely on resemblance to a typical or averaged category representation.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how typical examples can guide category decisions.

#### Reasoning and Problem Solving

Skills: 6

[reasoningAndProblemSolving.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/reasoningAndProblemSolving/reasoningAndProblemSolving.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** A person's representation of a challenge constrains which rules, heuristics, and solutions become available.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore psychological processes involved in reasoning and solving problems.

##### Deductive Reasoning

[deductiveReasoning.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/reasoningAndProblemSolving/skills/deductiveReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain drawing conclusions that follow from given premises, distinguishing actual human performance from formal validity.

**User-friendly description (en):** Distinguish conclusions that necessarily follow from stated premises.

##### Functional Fixedness

[functionalFixedness.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/reasoningAndProblemSolving/skills/functionalFixedness.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Identify how familiar uses of an object can inhibit a different effective use.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize when an object's familiar use blocks a new solution.

##### Inductive Reasoning

[inductiveReasoning.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/reasoningAndProblemSolving/skills/inductiveReasoning.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain generalizing beyond observed cases and why resulting conclusions remain uncertain.

**User-friendly description (en):** Recognize how examples support tentative broader conclusions.

##### Insight and Restructuring

[insightAndRestructuring.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/reasoningAndProblemSolving/skills/insightAndRestructuring.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain abrupt reinterpretation during problem solving without treating the feeling of insight as proof.

**User-friendly description (en):** Understand how changing a problem's representation can produce an insight.

##### Means–Ends Analysis

[meansEndsAnalysis.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/reasoningAndProblemSolving/skills/meansEndsAnalysis.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Describe selecting intermediate actions that reduce a discrepancy between a current state and a goal.

**User-friendly description (en):** Break the gap between the current state and a goal into manageable steps.

##### Problem Representation

[problemRepresentation.data.ts](../../../learningApps/psychology/data/skills/thinkingAndDecisionMaking/reasoningAndProblemSolving/skills/problemRepresentation.data.ts)

**Methodological description (English):** Explain how changing the formulation of a problem changes the possible solution search.

**User-friendly description (en):** Explore why defining the problem differently can reveal a solution.
